correctness.rationale: RESULT.md establishes each step of its infinite density squeeze, not merely a finite experiment. Coprime divisor factorization preserves a Zumkeller partition; z(1+zt) is Zumkeller. For fixed odd Zumkeller z, Dirichlet gives for each reduced class a mod z² a prime q_a≡a-z mod z² (reduced since gcd(a,z)=1); for n sufficiently large and coprime z, n-q_a=z+z²t is a positive Zumkeller number. Somu–Kukla–Tran Lemma 3.3 provides arbitrarily many disjoint sufficiently late odd prime-block Zumkeller numbers z_i. Minimal crossing gives R_i=∏(1+1/p)<8/3; ∏_{p|z_i}(1-p^-2)>2/3 (telescoping over all m≥3), hence φ(z_i)/z_i>1/4. CRT makes every fixed-r simultaneous noncoprimality set have density ∏(1-φ(z_i)/z_i)<(3/4)^r, proving upper density zero as r is arbitrary. The infinite claim uses the published prime-block theorem and Dirichlet, not verify.py outputs.
residual_risks: The deep published prime-block Zumkeller existence lemma is a cited primary theorem, not independently reproved here; all later deductions are checked. Finite partition tests cannot substitute for it.
